Zoning Change Application #22877-T1
SUBSTITUTE NARRATIVE AND PLANS FOR TYPE 1 ZONING AMENDMENT FOR
930 WEST HURON STREET, CHICAGO

The subject property is a Transit Served Location, as it is situated within 1,000” from the Blue
Line at Chicago Ave. and the Milwaukee Bus Corridor. It is currently improved with an older 3-
story industrial building. The Applicant intends to demolish the existing building and redevelop
this property with a new 6-story residential building with 35 dwelling units and 29 parking spaces
located in the garage and with a rooftop deck to be located on the principal building. The
Applicant needs a zoning change to a DR-5 Downtown Residential District with optional
variation and administrative adjustment relief for rear and front setback reduction, for elimination
of one loading berth, and to allow parking ratio in excess of 0.5 parking space per unit, to allow

residential use at the property and to comply with the standards and the bulk requirements of the
Ordinance for this redevelopment project.

Project Zoning Change from an MI-3 Limited Manufacturing/Business Park
Description: District to a DR-5 Downtown Residential District

Use: Residential Building with 35 Dwelling Units and 29 parking spaces.
Lot Area: 75' x 102'= 7,650 SF (recorded measurements)

Floor Area Ratio: | 5.0

Floor Area: 37,075 SF (see plans attached)

Density: 218.57 Square Feet per DU

Off- Street Parking: | Parking spaces: 29 (see administrative adjustment request below)

Setbacks: Front: 0°
Side: 1’ on the west side and 0°-4” on the east side

Rear: I (see variation request below)
Open Space: 1,823 SF

Building Height: | 72’-6 7/8” per the attached plans


L The applicant will comply with Section 17-4-0301 Specific Criteria for Transit-Served
Locations, should such provisions be determined as applicable:

17-4-0301 Specific Criteria for Transit-Served Locations. In D districts, any new construction
within 2,640 feet of a CTA or METRA rail station entrance or exit must satisfy all of the
following specific criteria:

1. The project complies with the applicable standards of Section 17-10-0102-B Transit-Served
Locations:

The subject property is a Transit Served Location, as it is located approximately 1,000 feet from
the Milwaukee Bus Corridor, and it is also located approximately 1,000 feet from the Chicago
Avenue Blue Line Train Station.

2. The project complies with the standards and regulations of Section 17-4-0504, except paragraph E
if the project is not located along a pedestrian street and except paragraph C if the land use is
designated in a non-commercial use group, pertaining to pedestrian streets and pedestrian retail
streets, even if the project is not located along a pedestrian street or a pedestrian retail street:

The subject property is not located along Pedestrian Street or Pedestrian Retail Street; however,
the project complies with the following criteria:

(a) The entire building fagade abuts the sidewalk or is located within 5 feet of the sidewalk.

(b) The requirements of Section 17-4-0504-C Transparency standards do not apply to the subject
development as proposed building is entirely residential (non-commercial use group) and there is
no commercial space which would require clear, non-reflective windows, and the project will not
provide any product display windows.

(c) The building will have a primary entrance door facing Huron Street.

(d) All off-street parking spaces will be located inside the principal building and will not be
visible from the right-of-way.

(e) The proposed parking will be located inside the building: in the basement and on the ground

floor; vehicle access to the parking area will come via the two proposed driveways, per site plan
attached.

3. The project complies with the general goals set forth in the Transit Friendly Development Guide:
Station Area Typology, and any other station-specific plans, designs or guidelines adopted by the
Chicago Plan Commission.

This Criteria is not applicable to this project.

4. Residential building projects shall not have a number of parking spaces in excess of 50% of the
Minimum Automobile Parking Ratio for the applicable district listed in Section 17-10-0208 with
any fractional result rounded up to the next higher whole number, unless additional parking spaces
are approved as an administrative adjustment under the provisions of Section 17-13-1003-EE; and

dy
A

With this proposed redevelopment, the Applicant is proposing a parking ratio which is in excess
of 50% of the Minimum Automobile Parking Ratio for the applicable district listed in Section 17-
10-0208. Consequently, the Applicant is requesting an Administrative Adjustment via Optional
Relief (see below) to increase the parking from 18 spaces required to 29 parking spaces proposed,
which is still less than 1:] parking ratio listed in Section 17-10-0208.

5. The project complies with the Travel Demand Study and Management Plan rules of the Chicago
Department of Transportation. The City's Commissioner of Transportation is authorized to issue
Travel Demand Study and Management Plan rules consistent with this section.

This Criteria is not applicable to this project.

Il. Optional Relief for Adjustment and Variation under Section 17-13-0303-D —

a Type 1 map amendment pursuant to Section 17-13-0300, may include relief available
pursuant to Section 17-13-1000 or 17-13-1100; in such instances, City Council approval of a
Type-1 application containing said elements shall preclude subsequent review otherwise
required pursuant to Sections 17-13-1000 or 17-13-1100, provided that no Type 1
application permits issued may be in violation of Section 17-13-0310:

(A) _ With this Type 1 Rezoning, the Applicant also seeks relief for Administrative Adjustment
under section 17-13-1003-EE, from the parking requirements of Section 17-4-0301(4) to
increase the on-site parking requirements from 18 parking spaces required to 29 parking
spaces, as proposed.

(B) The Applicant also seeks relief for variation under section 17-13-1101-B, from rear
setback requirements of Section 17-4-0406-B, which states that the minimum rear setback
for principal buildings other than detached houses is 30% of lot depth or 50 feet,
whichever is less. The required rear setback for principal buildings other than detached
houses, such as the proposed, applies only to those portions of a building that are 18 feet
or more above grade.

The Applicant also seeks relief for variation from front setback requirements of Section
17-4-0406-A, which states that buildings and structures in DR districts are subject to the R
district front setback standards of Sec. 17-2-0305.

To mitigate site planning hardships on this substandard lot, the Applicant requests a
reduction in the required rear setback from 30.6 feet required to 1 foot proposed; and to
line up with the existing improvements on this block (this is a corner property and the
adjacent properties to the west have zero front setback), if needed, reduction in the front
setback to zero feet proposed.

(C) The Applicant also seeks relief for variation under Section 17-13-1101-D, from the
loading requirements of Section 17-10-1101, to reduce the required number of loading
berth from one to zero.

(D) The Applicant is seeking all relief necessary, as allowed by the Zoning Ordinance, for
the proposed development per the attached Type 1 Plans.
